clue.text: Start of court proceedings

parts.note: on a tennis court every point opens with a serve, so the server's opening stroke begins play; the legal sense of court is the decoy

explanation.surface: A clerk announces that a trial is about to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the opening stroke of each point, which sets the play going on court, is the serve.

clue.text: After work, retire to a foreign country

indicators.note: once the letters have been worked, as clay is worked into a new shape, they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone plans to emigrate to Africa once their career ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After work' reads as 'once employment ends', but it says the letters of RETIRE A are to be worked into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is an independent state in the Horn of Africa, a foreign country to a British solver.

clue.text: He makes one cross at times

definitions.text: He makes one cross at times

parts.words: He makes one cross at times
parts.note: at an election a ballot paper is marked with an X, so this person makes a cross now and again rather than angering anyone

explanation.surface: A man occasionally annoys people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone casting a ballot marks a cross beside a candidate's name at each election.

clue.text: TV line between Britain and France

definitions.meaning: a television station broadcasting on its own frequency
the stretch of sea separating England from France, known as the English one

explanation.surface: A television network straddles the two nations.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster's station is a channel, and the sea strait dividing England from France is the English Channel.

clue.text: Wine cash bill is incorrect — fifty short

indicators.note: an incorrect bill has its letters wrongly ordered, telling us to rearrange them
short of means lacking, so the letter for fifty is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A diner's bill for the white wine is wrong and fifty pounds too little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the L from CASHBILL, leaving CASHBIL, which 'is incorrect' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white wine from the northern Burgundy region of France.

clue.text: He's engaged in outdoor pursuits

parts.note: pursuits read literally as chases of game in the open air, not as leisure hobbies

explanation.surface: A man enjoys hiking and other open-air hobbies.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who chases foxes or deer across country is literally engaged in outdoor pursuit.

clue.text: They provide power for gun emplacements

definitions.meaning: electric cells that store charge for devices
groups of artillery pieces set up together in a fortified position

explanation.surface: Something supplies energy to artillery positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry cells storing electricity share their name with the military word for a group of artillery guns.

clue.text: Clued in a way to take one in

indicators.note: the letters are put in a different way, an altered arrangement

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter explains how they let a solver into the secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CLUED IN, rearranged as 'a way' signals, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To include someone is to bring them into a group, to take them in as a member.

clue.text: Points out ripe possibilities of advancement

annotationWithheld.why: 'Points out ripe possibilities of advancement' (13): the anagram fodder needs every letter of 'Points out ripe', so 'out' would be both fodder and the only anagram indicator.
annotationWithheld.clue: Points out ripe possibilities of advancement

clue.text: Lean over table

definitions.meaning: to tilt to one side, as a ship does
a set of items written down in order

explanation.surface: Someone bends across a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels has a list, and a tabulated set of names or figures is also a list.

clue.text: Plane crash seen by store staff

indicators.note: a crashed plane is wrecked, so its letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a stock is a supply kept in store

explanation.surface: An aircraft goes down and the shop's employees witness it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is the definition: a long pole for climbing. 'crash' turns PLANE into ALPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenstock is a long iron-tipped walking stick used by mountaineers, a kind of staff.

clue.text: Rehearsal for a TT race?

definitions.meaning: a practice performance before the real event
TT is teetotal, so a race of abstainers would be one with no drink, a run that is dry

explanation.surface: Riders practise ahead of the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man, but TT also means teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress rehearsal or trial is a practice before the real thing; the query flags the teetotal pun.

clue.text: Revealed how one was less reserved?

definitions.meaning: disclosed or laid open to view
someone who has become more forthcoming about their feelings has unbent and talked freely

explanation.surface: A shy person disclosed how they became more outgoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To open something up is to expose it, and a person who opens up speaks frankly about themselves.

clue.text: Setting for new clock in the City?

indicators.note: the new letters sit inside the name of the city

parts.note: Bath is the Somerset spa city, the one named in many crossword clues

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so these letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new clock is installed somewhere in London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' suggests London's financial square mile but is BATH, a historic spa city in Somerset. 'new' makes CKCLO from CLOCK, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted cloth hung at the rear of a stage forms the scenery, the setting for the play.

clue.text: College girl found in Norfolk

parts.note: King's is a college of Cambridge University
Lynn is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman studying at a university is discovered in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is a county in eastern England; King's Lynn is a market town there.
explanation.definitionFit: King's Lynn is a port town on the Great Ouse in Norfolk, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Cover point keeps out of sight

parts.note: a hide is a skin, the covering of an animal
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A fielder in the cover point position stays hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover point is a fielding position in cricket, but here the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to keep it out of view, the sense the definition gives.

clue.text: Enormous soldier — a six-footer

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
an insect such as an ant has six feet

explanation.surface: A very tall soldier stands six feet high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall man but is an insect, which has six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something giant is huge, of enormous size, as the adjective says.

clue.text: An outcast, his meal is cooked for him

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered, and so are these letters

explanation.surface: Someone prepares food for a rejected person.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar, is cast out into the desert, so his name means an outcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical son of Hagar was sent away, and his name has come to stand for any outcast.

clue.text: I'm so taken aback by it in any display of ill-will

indicators.note: the inserted letters go inside the word any

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word so is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked by a show of hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns only the word 'so', not the whole of 'I'm so'; 'display' belongs with the definition, a show of ill feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is strong hostility, an open show of ill feeling toward someone.

clue.text: Music master

parts.note: an eminent conductor or composer, a master of music, rather than a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A teacher of music at school.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian word for master, used for a distinguished conductor or musician.

clue.text: About one thousand different paint drums

indicators.note: the anagram goes about, around, the other letters
made different, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Nearly a thousand different paints are on offer in drums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns PAINT into TPANI; 'About' puts it around IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are the kettledrums of an orchestra, the set of tuned drums.

clue.text: Joins military formations around the East

indicators.note: the formations are placed around the letter for East

parts.note: units are formations of an army
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: An army merges its divisions in the eastern theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to bring them together, to join them as one.

clue.text: Wooden horse

definitions.meaning: made of the timber of the sweet or horse ... tree

explanation.surface: The Trojan horse made of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture of chestnut timber is chestnut, and a reddish-brown horse is also called by the name.

clue.text: Puzzle set in game

indicators.note: letters that are set are arranged in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A riddle is included in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' reads as placed but rearranges IN GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a riddle or mystery, a puzzle to be solved.

clue.text: Batting cricket side to pocket the ball

parts.note: a side that is batting in cricket is in
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A team at the crease tries to send the ball away.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker or billiards an in-off is a shot where the ball goes into a pocket off another ball. The off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman's bat side.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiards shot that sends the cue ball into a pocket after striking another ball is called an in-off.

clue.text: Simple way of affluent living

parts.note: easy means simple
a street is a way, a road

explanation.surface: An uncomplicated route to a wealthy life.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on easy street is an idiom for a life of comfort and wealth.

clue.text: Love girl's curved shape

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, shown as O
Val is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman's beloved has a rounded figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is also a London cricket ground, but here it is just the egg-like shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-like outline is a closed curve, a shape that is oval.

clue.text: Complaint I will put before the head

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in front of the second

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness

explanation.surface: Someone vows to take a grievance to the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the head' suggests a school head but is NESS, a promontory jutting into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment, a sickness one suffers from.

clue.text: Concede well contains fish

indicators.note: the word for well holds the fish inside it

parts.note: fit means well, healthy
the orfe is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A healthy angler gives up after catching a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up something as a penalty or in a game is to concede it.
